The basic law of U.S. foreign aid. It separated economic from military assistance, set the purposes and conditions of each, and led President Kennedy to create the U.S. Agency for International Development by executive order two months later.

::: {.official-links}
**Read the law** (official GovInfo text)

[Enacted text: 75 Stat. 424](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/statute/75/424){.btn-official} [Current U.S. Code: 22 U.S.C. 2151 et seq.](https://www.govinfo.gov/link/uscode/22/2151?link-type=html){.btn-official}
:::

## Key provisions

- Part I: development assistance, including health, education, democracy, and disaster relief authorities.
- Part II: security assistance, including the Economic Support Fund, military education and training, peacekeeping, and Section 506 drawdown authority.
- Secs. 116 and 502B: human rights conditions on economic and security assistance.
- Sec. 620 and following: country and conduct restrictions, including the Cuba embargo authority in Sec. 620(a).
- Sec. 634A: advance notice to Congress before funds are reprogrammed.

## Why it matters

Most later aid and security assistance law is written as an amendment or companion to this act: the [Leahy Laws](leahy-laws.qmd), the [Symington-Glenn Amendments](symington-glenn.qmd), the [Hughes-Ryan Amendment](hughes-ryan-1974.qmd), the [Global Fragility Act](gfa-2019.qmd), and the military sales side that became the [Arms Export Control Act](aeca-1976.qmd). Its age and accumulated amendments are a common argument for rewriting it.

## Current status

In force. It has not had a comprehensive reauthorization since 1985, so foreign aid policy is mostly set through annual appropriations acts.

## Where it sits

- **Layer.** Framework statute. Standing laws that create institutions or general procedures other laws and executive actions plug into, such as the National Security Act, the War Powers Resolution, IEEPA, and FISA. ([How the layers work](../study/index.qmd#the-authority-stack))
- **Builds on.** [Mutual Security Act](mutual-security-1951.qmd).
- **Built upon by.** [Hughes-Ryan Amendment](hughes-ryan-1974.qmd), [Leahy Laws](leahy-laws.qmd), [Global Fragility Act](gfa-2019.qmd), [Symington-Glenn Amendments](symington-glenn.qmd), [Helms-Burton Act](helms-burton-1996.qmd).
- **Codified in.** [Title 22 U.S.C.](title22-usc.qmd).
- **Era.** Building the national security state ([timeline](../study/timeline.qmd)).
- **Study.** [Unit 9: Foreign assistance, fragility, and partners](../study/units/assistance.qmd) (core reading).
- **Member lenses.** [Rep. Sara Jacobs](../members/jacobs.qmd): Foreign Affairs; Security Sector Compacts Act.
